# source-links Specification

## Purpose

Defines how the server produces links into the POLITEMall and NYP Brightspace sites and the STEP portal that a user
can open to check what a tool told them: which pages exist for which kinds of item, how a link
is built and validated, and how the links are proven to work before and after release.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Links are generated by the server, never supplied by a model or by D2L data
Every link the server returns as evidence (`sourceUrl` or `pageUrl`) SHALL be produced by the
server from a fixed, verified page pattern, the school the data came from, and identifiers the
server read from D2L while serving that same request. Text fields that D2L returns (announcement
bodies, descriptions, topic URLs written by instructors) SHALL NOT be copied into an evidence
link field.

#### Scenario: link built from ids read in the same request
- **WHEN** a tool returns an announcement it just read from D2L
- **THEN** that announcement's `sourceUrl` SHALL point at the announcement page for exactly that announcement id in exactly that course

#### Scenario: an instructor-authored URL is not promoted to evidence
- **WHEN** an announcement body contains `https://example.com/anything`
- **THEN** that URL SHALL appear only inside the body text and SHALL NOT appear in any `sourceUrl` or `pageUrl`

### Requirement: Links only point at the site the data came from
An evidence link SHALL use `https`, SHALL use the host of the system the data was read from
(`nyplms.polite.edu.sg` for NYP, `lms.polite.edu.sg` for POLITEMall, `stms.polite.edu.sg` for
STEP), and SHALL contain nothing but the page path and the identifiers that page requires
(numeric for Brightspace, GUIDs for STEP). It SHALL NOT contain a
token, cookie, session value, user name, email address or any other credential or personal
identifier.

#### Scenario: host follows the system
- **WHEN** a cross-school tool returns one NYP item and one POLITEMall item
- **THEN** the NYP item's link SHALL be on `nyplms.polite.edu.sg` and the POLITEMall item's on `lms.polite.edu.sg`
- **WHEN** a STEP tool returns a course
- **THEN** its link SHALL be on `stms.polite.edu.sg`

#### Scenario: a link never carries a secret
- **WHEN** any tool result is inspected
- **THEN** no link in it SHALL contain the caller's MCP token, a session cookie value, or a user id

### Requirement: Item links open the exact item
For each of the following kinds of item the server SHALL provide a link that, for a signed-in
user who can see the item, opens that item's own page: course, announcement, content topic,
discussion topic, assignment (dropbox folder), quiz, survey and calendar event (Brightspace), and
enrolled course and catalogue course (STEP).

#### Scenario: announcement
- **WHEN** a user opens an announcement's `sourceUrl` while signed in to the right school
- **THEN** the page's title SHALL contain that announcement's title

#### Scenario: assignment and quiz
- **WHEN** a user opens an assignment's or quiz's `sourceUrl`
- **THEN** the page's title SHALL contain the assignment's or quiz's name

#### Scenario: STEP enrolled course
- **WHEN** a user opens the `sourceUrl` of a course returned by `list_step_courses`, `get_step_course_detail` or `get_step_timetable`
- **THEN** the rendered page SHALL show that course's name and its session timetable

#### Scenario: STEP catalogue course
- **WHEN** a user opens the `sourceUrl` of a course returned by `search_step_courses`
- **THEN** the rendered page SHALL show that course's name, and the link SHALL have been built from the catalogue entry's own item id, not its course id

#### Scenario: content topic in either content interface
- **WHEN** a user opens a content topic's `sourceUrl` for a course that uses the Lessons interface, or one that uses the enhanced sequence viewer
- **THEN** the page SHALL open that topic in either case, and the topic id SHALL be preserved in the final address

### Requirement: D2L-supplied view URLs are preferred where the identifier cannot be constructed
Where D2L returns its own view URL for an item and that URL uses an identifier other than the
item's own id (calendar events), the server SHALL use D2L's URL instead of building one, after
confirming it is `https`, on the same tenant host, and a path on that site.

#### Scenario: calendar event
- **WHEN** a tool returns a calendar event whose D2L data includes a view URL on the correct tenant
- **THEN** the event's `sourceUrl` SHALL be that URL

#### Scenario: a D2L-supplied URL on another host is discarded
- **WHEN** a D2L view URL points at a host other than the school's tenant
- **THEN** the server SHALL emit no `sourceUrl` for that item and SHALL NOT pass the foreign URL through

### Requirement: Where no item page exists the closest verified parent page is linked, or nothing
For data without its own page the server SHALL link the closest verified page that shows it,
identified as a `pageUrl` rather than an item `sourceUrl`; where no verified page shows it the
server SHALL emit no link.

#### Scenario: grades
- **WHEN** a tool returns the caller's grade items or final grade
- **THEN** the result SHALL carry the course's "my grades" page as `pageUrl` and SHALL NOT carry a per-grade-item link

#### Scenario: rubrics, course overview, classlist
- **WHEN** a tool returns rubrics
- **THEN** the link SHALL be the page of the assignment or discussion topic the rubric is attached to
- **WHEN** a tool returns a course overview
- **THEN** the link SHALL be the course home page
- **WHEN** a tool returns a classlist
- **THEN** the link SHALL be the course's classlist page and there SHALL be no link per person

#### Scenario: cross-course feeds
- **WHEN** a tool returns due, overdue or unread-activity rows across courses
- **THEN** each row SHALL link its course's home page and the result SHALL link the school's home page

### Requirement: A link points at the page that actually shows the data returned
A link SHALL be emitted only to a page that displays the same data the tool returned. Where a
system has two different sources that a user would call by the same name, the tool SHALL link
the page that shows the source it actually read, and SHALL NOT link a page that shows a
different one.

#### Scenario: STEP announcements
- **WHEN** `get_step_announcements` returns the portal banner announcements
- **THEN** its `pageUrl` SHALL be the STEP home page, where that banner is displayed, and SHALL NOT be the Announcements page, which lists a different set

#### Scenario: STEP timetable
- **WHEN** `get_step_timetable` returns a course's sessions
- **THEN** its link SHALL be that course's details page, which lists those sessions, with the calendar page available as a parent `pageUrl`

### Requirement: Links respect the caller's permissions
An instructor-only page SHALL be linked only from a tool that itself requires that permission,
and a link SHALL NOT be a means of reaching anything the caller's D2L role cannot already open.

#### Scenario: grader-only tool
- **WHEN** a Tutor or instructor calls a tool that only a grading role can use successfully (class grades, all final grades, quiz results, survey results)
- **THEN** the result's `pageUrl` SHALL be the corresponding management or list page for that course

#### Scenario: tool used by both audiences
- **WHEN** a tool that returns different scopes to different roles (dropbox submissions) is called
- **THEN** the management page SHALL be linked only if the caller's role in that course is a grading role, and otherwise the learner-facing page of the same item SHALL be linked

#### Scenario: a learner follows an instructor link
- **WHEN** a user without the required role opens an instructor page link
- **THEN** D2L SHALL answer with its own "not authorised" page (no data is exposed by the link)

### Requirement: Only verified link patterns are emitted
A link pattern SHALL be emitted only after it has been opened in a signed-in session on each
system where the pattern applies and shown to (a) return the page rather than an error or a
sign-in redirect, and (b) identify the item — by the item's name in the page title where the
page is titled by item, by the item id surviving in the final address where it is not, or, for a
single-page application that returns success and a generic title for any address (STEP), by the
item's name appearing in the rendered page content and no not-found message appearing. A blank
or empty render SHALL count as a failure. A pattern that has not been verified, or that fails
re-verification, SHALL NOT be emitted.

#### Scenario: STEP wrong id renders a message
- **WHEN** a STEP course-details link is opened with a course id that does not exist
- **THEN** the rendered page shows a not-found message, and verification SHALL treat that as the expected failure for a wrong-id control

#### Scenario: STEP wrong kind of id renders nothing
- **WHEN** a STEP catalogue link is opened with a course id where the item id is required
- **THEN** the page renders no course and no error, and verification SHALL treat a blank render as a failure of that pattern

#### Scenario: STEP courses at other institutes
- **WHEN** a STEP enrolled course belongs to an institute other than NYP, none of which could be tested
- **THEN** the server SHALL still build the link from the course's own institute value, and the verification report SHALL list institutes covered so the gap is visible

#### Scenario: verified on one school only
- **WHEN** a pattern has been verified on NYP but not on POLITEMall (no suitable item exists there to test)
- **THEN** the server SHALL emit that pattern's links for NYP data only, and SHALL emit none for POLITEMall data until it is verified there

#### Scenario: unverified item-level instructor pages
- **WHEN** no item was available to verify an item-level instructor page (folder submissions, quiz attempts, survey results)
- **THEN** the server SHALL link the verified management or list page instead

#### Scenario: a pattern fails re-verification
- **WHEN** re-verification of a pattern returns an error page or a title that does not identify the item
- **THEN** the verification run SHALL report the failure with the pattern, the school and the observed page, and the pattern SHALL be treated as blocked until fixed

### Requirement: Link verification can be re-run against real sessions on demand
The project SHALL provide a repeatable check that collects every link the curated tools return
for a known set of items, opens each in a signed-in session for the right system (rendering the
page for STEP), and reports
per link whether it opened correctly and identified the item. It SHALL also open a deliberately
wrong identifier for each item kind to confirm a wrong link is visibly an error rather than a
different item.

#### Scenario: full run
- **WHEN** the check is run against NYP and POLITEMall sessions
- **THEN** it SHALL report a pass or a specific failure for every returned link and for every wrong-identifier control

#### Scenario: no session
- **WHEN** a school or STEP has no signed-in session available
- **THEN** the check SHALL report that system's links as unverified rather than passing them
